locations.label: Nose (Nasal Subunits)
ladderSummary: Bilobed / dorsal nasal local flap (<1.5 cm)

locations.label: Oral Cavity / Tongue / Floor of Mouth
ladderSummary: Free RFFF or thin ALT / MSAP

locations.label: Mandible (Segmental Composite)
ladderSummary: Free DCIA or scapular osteocutaneous flap

locations.label: Sacrum, Spine & Ischium (Pressure Injuries)
ladderSummary: Gluteal V-Y advancement / SGAP / IGAP / Gluteal rotation

locations.label: Hand, Wrist & Digits
ladderSummary: Local: Atasoy V-Y, Moberg, Cross-finger, Kite (FDMA)
Regional: Reverse RFFF, PIA, Pedicled Groin
Free: Thin ALT, Lateral arm, MSAP, Toe-to-hand, Venous flap

locations.label: Elbow & Forearm
ladderSummary: Local / Reverse lateral arm / Pedicled LD

locations.label: Groin & Perineum / Pelvis
ladderSummary: Local: Pudendal thigh (Singapore) / Gluteal fold / Martius
Regional: Pedicled Gracilis, Pedicled VRAM, Pedicled ALT

locations.label: Leg — Proximal Third & Knee
ladderSummary: Medial or lateral gastrocnemius muscle flap (workhorse)

locations.label: Leg — Middle Third Tibia
ladderSummary: Posterior tibial / Peroneal perforator propeller flap
Free ALT / Gracilis / LD (high-energy Gustilo IIIB)

locations.label: Leg — Distal Third, Ankle & Heel
ladderSummary: Free ALT, Gracilis, RFFF, MSAP, or Fibula (gold standard for Gustilo IIIB)

locations.label: Foot — Plantar Heel & Weight-Bearing Surface
ladderSummary: Medial plantar artery (instep) neurovascular flap (gold standard glabrous sensate)
Reverse sural neurocutaneous flap (non-weight-bearing posterior heel)
Free thin sensate ALT / RFFF / Gracilis + STSG (massive plantar loss)

locations.label: Neck & Supraclavicular Region
ladderSummary: Pedicled Latissimus dorsi or Supraclavicular flap

locations.label: Shoulder & Proximal Arm
ladderSummary: Local advancement / STSG if muscle bed intact
Pedicled Latissimus dorsi or TDAP flap (workhorse)

presets.title: Lower Extremity — Distal Third Tibia (Gustilo IIIB)
presets.subtitle: Exposed distal tibia & hardware, 12 × 7 cm, out of reach of soleus
ladderSteps: 1. Exclude primary closure & STSG (exposed bone/hardware)
2. Local propeller / reverse sural only if small & outside zone of injury
3. Free tissue transfer (ALT, Gracilis, MSAP, or LD) is workhorse for distal third

presets.title: Autologous Total Breast Reconstruction
presets.subtitle: Post-mastectomy irradiated chest wall, soft natural mound needed
ladderSteps: 1. Gold standard abdominal donor: DIEP (muscle-sparing) > MS-TRAM > SIEA (if caliber ≥1.5 mm)
2. Alternative donor sites if abdomen unavailable: PAP, TUG, SGAP/IGAP
3. Pedicled salvage: Extended LD / TDAP (± implant)

presets.title: Head & Neck — Segmental Mandibular Composite Defect
presets.subtitle: 10 cm segmental mandibular osteotomy + floor-of-mouth mucosa defect
ladderSteps: 1. Vascularized bone is mandatory for anterior/long-segment defects
2. Free Fibula Osteocutaneous flap is primary workhorse (up to 25 cm bone)
3. Alternatives: Free DCIA (iliac crest) or Scapular osteocutaneous flap

presets.title: Lower Extremity — Proximal Third / Knee Exposed Prosthesis
presets.subtitle: Exposed patellar tendon and proximal tibial metaphysis, 8 × 6 cm
ladderSteps: 1. Medial (or lateral) gastrocnemius muscle flap + STSG is gold standard
2. Pedicled MSAP if skin-only thin coverage preferred
3. Free ALT / LD if gastrocnemius injured or massive defect

presets.title: Lower Extremity — Middle Third Tibia Exposed Fracture
presets.subtitle: 9 × 6 cm exposed mid-shaft tibia with local soleus muscle intact
ladderSteps: 1. Medial hemisoleus or soleus muscle flap + STSG is classic regional workhorse
2. Posterior tibial or peroneal perforator propeller flap for small-to-moderate defects
3. Free ALT / Gracilis if high-energy trauma crushed the soleus muscle

presets.title: Major Nasal Subunit Reconstruction (>2 cm)
presets.subtitle: Full-thickness nasal tip and dorsum defect after Mohs excision
ladderSteps: 1. Defects <1.5 cm: Bilobed or local advancement flap
2. Defects >1.5–2 cm or multiple subunits: Paramedian forehead flap (gold standard)
3. Cartilage framework + mucosal lining as needed; staged pedicle division at 3 weeks

presets.title: Deep Sternal Wound Infection / Mediastinitis
presets.subtitle: Post-sternotomy dehiscence with exposed sternum and dead space
ladderSteps: 1. Serial debridement & negative-pressure wound therapy
2. Bilateral pectoralis major advancement or turnover flaps (workhorse)
3. Lower sternal third: Rectus abdominis (VRAM) or Omental flap

presets.title: Stage IV Sacral Pressure Injury
presets.subtitle: 10 × 8 cm sacral ulcer with exposed sacrum after osteomyelitis debridement
ladderSteps: 1. Nutritional optimization, offloading, bony prominence ostectomy
2. Gluteal rotation / V-Y fasciocutaneous / SGAP perforator flap (preserve future options)
3. Avoid sacrificing gluteus maximus function in ambulatory patients

presets.title: Dorsal Hand Defect with Exposed Extensor Tendons
presets.subtitle: 8 × 5 cm dorsal hand avulsion requiring thin gliding coverage
ladderSteps: 1. Regional pedicled: Posterior interosseous (PIA), Reverse RFFF, or staged Groin flap
2. Single-stage free thin flap: RFFF, thin ALT, Lateral arm, or MSAP
3. Fascial flap (TPFF) + STSG for ultra-thin tendon gliding

presets.title: Scalp & Calvarium Oncologic Defect (Irradiated)
presets.subtitle: 14 × 11 cm scalp resection with exposed calvarium & dura/hardware
ladderSteps: 1. Exclude primary closure & STSG (exposed denuded calvarium / radiated bed)
2. Free ALT (thin fascia/skin) or Free Latissimus Dorsi muscle + STSG (massive contour)
3. Superficial temporal vessels are primary recipients; consider vein graft if scarred

presets.title: Abdominal Wall Composite Full-Thickness Defect
presets.subtitle: 15 × 10 cm radiated full-thickness abdominal wall resection with fascial loss
ladderSteps: 1. Component separation + biologic/synthetic mesh if skin intact
2. Pedicled or Free ALT with vascularized fascia lata for dynamic fascial reconstruction
3. Alternatives: Free Latissimus dorsi or contralateral VRAM

presets.title: Plantar Heel Weight-Bearing Surface Defect
presets.subtitle: 6 × 5 cm exposed calcaneus on weight-bearing heel requiring sensate glabrous skin
ladderSteps: 1. Medial plantar artery (instep) neurovascular flap is gold standard (like-with-like glabrous sensate)
2. Reverse sural neurocutaneous flap if instep donor unavailable (non-glabrous)
3. Free sensate ALT / RFFF / Gracilis + STSG for massive plantar loss
